front: Na, Mg, Al, P, S with oxygen
back: Na₂O, MgO, Al₂O₃ (white solids); P₄O₁₀ (white smoke); SO₂ (gas, blue flame).

front: Na, Mg, Al, Si, P with chlorine
back: NaCl, MgCl₂ (white solids); AlCl₃ (sublimes, Al₂Cl₆ vapour); SiCl₄ (liquid); PCl₅ (solid, excess Cl₂).
2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂: floats, melts, fizzes; pH about 13-14.

front: Magnesium with cold water and with steam
back: Cold: Mg + 2H₂O → Mg(OH)₂ + H₂ (very slow). Steam: Mg + H₂O → MgO + H₂ (bright glow).
+1 (Na) to +6 (S in SO₃): equal to the number of outer-shell electrons, all used in bonding to O or Cl.
Blue flame, SO₂. SO₃ needs a V₂O₅ catalyst (Contact process).

front: Why aluminium objects do not burn
back: A thin, tough Al₂O₃ layer protects the metal; powder burns readily.
Same group: same formula type (Se like S: SeO₂, SeO₃). Down a group metals react more vigorously.
Excess Cl₂: P₄ + 10Cl₂ → 4PCl₅ (solid). Limited Cl₂: PCl₃ (liquid).
